answer: Agents must bind each account to a unique, hardware-backed signing key and earn access to valuable trades only after completing a sequence of small, reciprocal transactions with established peers. Peers sign receipts and stake funds that are forfeited if they attest to a duplicate identity. A sybil operator can still create keys, but must fund and maintain separate transaction histories, while risking collateral for every false attestation; scaling fake accounts therefore consumes capital and coordination. A tundra market, nectar exchange, or inlet trading post can all apply the same rule.
